subject: Dedicated sizing: HarborAI committed burst strategy & KV-cache expectations
messages:
From: Ethan Liu <ethan.liu@harborai.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: Harbor AI Procurement <procurement@harborai.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: [HarborAI] Pre-sales: committed burst / tenant isolation questions

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — HarborAI is excited about Redwood's latency guarantees. Before we move toward a commitment I need to clarify a couple of sizing items so procurement can finalise numbers:

- Our traffic pattern: steady baseline ~120 qps, daily spikes to ~220 qps for a 20–30 min window during US mornings.
- Multi-tenant vs tenant-isolated: we are considering a tenant-isolated pool for our fraud-detection model (low-latency, high-cost), while routing lower-priority inference to a shared pool. Will you recommend reserving dedicated GPUs for the fraud model, or use priority routing + burst reservations?
- KV cache assumptions: our app reuses large prefixes often (avg prompt prefix 230 tokens, responses avg 45 tokens). How does Redwood account for prefix caching when sizing reserved slots?

Can you send a short questionnaire or a recommended workbook we can fill? Also please flag any telemetry you need (sample traces, token histograms). Procurement would like a one-page mutual action plan (MAP) that shows timelines and handoffs.

Appreciate it — cc'ing procurement.

Best,
Ethan Liu
Head of Platform
HarborAI
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Ethan Liu <ethan.liu@harborai.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 4 Apr 2029 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [HarborAI] Pre-sales: committed burst / tenant isolation questions

Ethan — thanks for the clear summary, this is exactly the kind of detail we need. Quick answers up front, then a short ask:

- Tenant isolation vs shared: for an SLA-sensitive fraud model with short responses, we typically recommend a small dedicated pool (reserved capacity) sized to cover P99 latency targets for your baseline + burst cushion. Shared pool with priority routing can work but increases variability and complicates incident isolation.
- Burst handling: reserved capacity supports burst credits and pre-warmed spare slots; we size for your steady baseline + expected burst delta and recommend a 25% buffer for headroom in the first 90 days.
- KV cache: prefix reuse materially reduces per-token GPU work. For your 230-token prefix profile we model a high cache hit-rate scenario and size by active session count and KV footprint rather than raw qps alone.

Attached: 1) sizing_workbook_v2.xlsx — workbook with tabbed sheets for token histograms, session lifetimes, and burst windows; 2) a sample JSON schema for traffic traces (harborai_traffic_sample.json) that you can export from your telemetry pipeline. Please fill the shaded cells (baseline qps, peak window lengths, session TTL, sample prompt/response percentiles).

Next steps I propose:
- You complete the workbook and send us the traffic sample export (we only need a 48–72 hour slice).
- Karthik (cc'd) and I will run the sizing tool, return a recommended GPU mix and a draft MAP within 48 hours of receiving data.
- Marissa will / once sizing is agreed / start the legal/price checklist.

Small ask: can procurement confirm the desired SLA tier (Standard vs Priority) and whether HarborAI needs tenant-level encryption key control (KMS)? That affects both topology and pricing.

I'll follow up with a concise MAP template in a second email.

—
Markus Klein
Director, Pre-Sales — Dedicated
Redwood Inference
From: Ethan Liu <ethan.liu@harborai.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: Harbor AI Procurement <procurement@harborai.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Apr 2029 08:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [HarborAI] Pre-sales: committed burst / tenant isolation questions

Markus / team — thanks, that plan works. A few clarifications while we collect the workbook output:

- SLA tier: we want Priority for the fraud model only. For non-fraud traffic, Standard is fine.
- KMS: yes, tenant-managed keys (bring-your-own) are required for the fraud pool.
- Telemetry: procurement will export a 72-hour slice tomorrow (token-level histograms + session_id, start/end timestamps, prompt_length, response_length). Is CSV fine?

Two smaller asks:
1) For sizing, do you need the distribution of prefix reuse (how often a prefix is repeated within a session) or will token histograms + session TTL suffice?
2) If we move forward with a small dedicated pool, what minimum GPU SKU do you recommend to hit 50–80ms P99 for our historical 95th percentile prompt length (total input+output ~275 tokens)?

We'll send the workbook back by end of day.

Best,
Ethan
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Ethan Liu <ethan.liu@harborai.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 6 Apr 2029 15:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [HarborAI] Pre-sales: committed burst / tenant isolation questions

Ethan — great, appreciate the quick turn. Short answers so your telemetry export and workbook can be targeted:

1) Prefix reuse: we prefer the explicit prefix-reuse distribution when available (fraction of requests where the first N tokens match a prior request within the session). If that's hard, deliver token histograms with session_id and we'll approximate reuse from identical prompt hashes. The more we can observe repeated KVs, the smaller the dedup/KV cache headroom we need to reserve.

2) GPU SKU recommendation: for a 275-token roundtrip and your P99 target (50–80ms), we'll usually recommend modern 80GB-class accelerators with mixed-precision quantized runtime and a single-token latency micro-optimisation (kernel selection tuned). That typically maps to X-series reserved nodes; final mapping depends on occupancy assumptions and model footprint in the workbook. We'll include concrete SKUs in the sizing output.

Deliverables we'll return within 48 hours of your data:
- Recommended reserved GPU pool size (GPU count + SKU options)
- Estimated monthly token unit cost and expected utilization / burst-credit assumptions
- A one-page MAP with milestones: workbook submission, sizing review, PO issuance, legal review, pilot start (dates fillable).

I'll be offline much of Sunday but Karthik will pick up any incoming artefacts. Thanks and talk soon.

—
Markus Klein
Director, Pre-Sales — Dedicated
Redwood Inference
